environment.description: Same ASP.NET Core 7.0 API deployed on AKS (Azure Kubernetes Service) behind an nginx-ingress controller configured with annotation nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client set to 'on' and auth-tls-secret pointing to a CA bundle (namespace/client-ca-secret) containing only the internal PKI root CA. The ingress resource specifies auth-tls-verify-depth of 2 and auth-tls-pass-certificate-to-upstream-header is enabled. The nginx-ingress controller terminates mTLS at the edge — connections without a valid client certificate signed by the internal CA receive HTTP 400 (No required SSL certificate was sent) before any request bytes reach the application pod. The AKS cluster uses a NetworkPolicy (Calico CNI) restricting ingress to the pod only from the ingress-controller namespace on port 8080, preventing any bypass via direct pod IP. The internal PKI CA is an offline root with intermediate issuance only to registered service accounts via HashiCorp Vault PKI secrets engine with a max_ttl of 24h and required CN matching pattern 'svc-*.internal.corp'.

config.network_policy: deny-all-ingress except from namespace ingress-system on port 8080
config.pki: HashiCorp Vault PKI engine, offline root CA, intermediate issues certs with CN=svc-*.internal.corp, max_ttl=24h
config.client_cert_issuance: only via Vault role bound to Kubernetes service accounts in approved namespaces
